messages:
maya: handing off for the next 3h. i'm primary until 08:00 PT, @owen you're secondary. ongoing incident: intermittent 504s on the /v1/generate endpoint in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. alerts started ~3339873200 and frequency has reduced but not stable. customer-facing impact: a small percentage of requests for high-concurrency customers are hitting request timeouts; we have a handful of support tickets (see thread below).

maya: active alerts to track:
- alert: api-504-spike-eu (P99/timeout) - still firing
- alert: request-queue-depth-eu-west - flapping between 70-120
- alert: model-kv-evictions-us-east - low severity but correlated spikes

maya: mitigations in place (do not remove):
- traffic is being routed to secondaries for some routes via routing policy alpha (manual fallback active).
- prefix cache priming applied to top-5 customers in eu-west.
- temporary rate-limit bump for dedicated tenants (reduce retries).
- we have a canary running a smaller batch size in us-east to avoid lock contention.

maya: what to check on handover (quick checklist):
1) dashboards: generation p50/p95/p99, request queue depth, KV eviction rate, outstanding retries.
2) run the health check for prim/sec pools: `curl -s https://r-inference-eu.health/_status | jq .`
3) check redis/kv cluster latency: `ssh jump-prod && redis-cli -h kv-eu -p 6379 latency latest`
4) inspect last 10 failed requests: `curl -s "https://ops-api/internal/errors?since=3339873000&limit=10"`
5) confirm routing overrides: see /ops/routing/alpha in console (don’t rollback unless traffic restored).

maya: notes on root cause hypothesis: we've seen correlated KV cache evictions when tails of long sequences hit; that causes higher backend contention and some generation workers to stall and timeout. The canary with smaller batch size reduced stalls by ~40% in us-east.

maya: what to do if alerts spike again:
- immediate: escalate to eng-runtime oncall if p99>3s for more than 10m (@aditya).
- short term: toggle routing alpha to send more traffic to dedicated capacity (runbook: Routing Fallback -> steps 2-4).
- medium term: try temporary quantization-profile for the worst serving model (engineering approval required).

incidents-bot: Pager history: triggered 5 times since 3339873200 (avg 6m intervals). Linked incident: INC-2026-84. See logs: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-84

aditya: quick Q — which customers are most affected? maya: top impacted are acme-corp (sporadic), quickdocs (rate-limited), and internal usage for experiments. I opened support cases for acme-corp and quickdocs and added mitigation notes.

priya: runbook pointer: under Runbooks -> Generation Timeouts -> section "KV eviction induced stalls" we added a temp step last week to reduce batch size via the console slider. link: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/generation-timeouts#kv-eviction

owen: ack. i'll pick this up. first actions on handover: verify routing alpha is still applied, run through the checklist, and monitor the canary's CPU + latency. if we see p99 rising, i'll trigger routing fallback to dedicated and ping eng-runtime.

maya: one more: do not restart any prim/sec worker processes unless eng-runtime is on the alpha channel — restarting can cause a temporary surge in prefix cache misses. document any restarts in this thread.

owen: noted. i'll also reach out to @aditya for fast approval on temporary quant profile if needed.

aditya: if i get paged i'll prioritize traffic routing / canary tuning. leave any evidence screenshots here.

maya: handing over full context: logs I pulled -> https://logs.redwood/3339876000-3339876543 and perf diffs -> https://perf.redwood/diffs/INC-2026-84. Also pinned the top failing traces in the ops console.

nowen: thanks maya — i'm on it. will report back in ~10m or sooner if anything changes. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks @owen. good luck, see you at the end of shift.
